claude_proposed_widenings.name: ActivationPhase.unconditional
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Power Word Heal applies its effects to the target unconditionally — no attack roll, no saving throw. The existing ActivationPhase union only has attack_roll and save_gate. An unconditional phase variant is needed to express spells that fire effects directly on a target without a roll.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: A wave of healing energy washes over one creature you can see within range.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: DiceAmount.restore_all
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The heal amount is 'regains all its Hit Points' — a full restore to max HP, not a dice expression. DiceAmount only supports fixed dice expressions, threshold tiers, and linear-per-level progressions. None can encode a 'set HP to maximum' semantic. A new variant such as { kind: 'restore_all' } is required.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: The target regains all its Hit Points.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: SpellEffect.heal_hp
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: HealHpEffect exists in ClassFeatureEffect but is not part of the spell Effect union (Effect = DamageEffect | NoneEffect). Spells cannot currently express a heal effect at all. Power Word Heal's primary mechanic is healing, so the heal_hp effect must be promoted into the spell Effect union.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: The target regains all its Hit Points.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: SpellEffect.remove_condition
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Power Word Heal ends Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, and Stunned conditions unconditionally on the target. The v4 atom 'remove_condition' exists in the taxonomy but there is no surface variant in the spell Effect type to encode it. A RemoveConditionEffect variant is needed in the spell Effect union.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: If the creature has the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, or Stunned condition, the condition ends.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: SpellEffect.grant_reaction_use
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The Prone clause grants the target permission to use its Reaction to stand up — a secondary effect that opens a reaction window for a specific move action. This is not expressible with any existing effect variant. It is a secondary rider and the narrowest pressure; could be modeled as a note or omitted in a first-pass widening, but it is genuinely missing.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: If the creature has the Prone condition, it can use its Reaction to stand up.
